title: Sky remediates deprecated emissions by burning back to the counterfactual supply, not merely by stopping them
content:
A.4.1.2.2.4.1 describes replacing emissions-funded SKY Rewards with rewards paid from SKY the protocol already holds. Stopping the emissions would have been the obvious fix; the Atlas records a stronger one. "SKY tokens equal to the total SKY emissions previously used to fund SKY Rewards, including the Early Bird Reward, were burned from SKY held by the Sky Protocol," and the stated goal is explicit: "The combination of these actions achieved a state where the number of total SKY tokens is exactly the same as if SKY Rewards had never been funded with protocol emissions."

A.4.1.2.2.4.2 applies the identical treatment to the conversion path. The Legacy Conversion Contract minted new SKY; the New Conversion Contract issues from preminted supply instead. "To offset SKY minted by the Legacy Conversion Contract after the deployment of the New Conversion Contract, an equivalent amount of preminted SKY was burned. This action ensured the total SKY token supply remains as if these specific emissions from the Legacy Conversion Contract had not occurred."

The repeated phrase — *as if it had never occurred* — is the pattern. The remediation target is not "stop the leak" but "restore the counterfactual." That is a much stricter standard, and it is only reachable because the protocol holds a burnable SKY balance to net against.

Why it matters: under a no-new-emissions rule, credibility depends on there being no grandfathered exceptions. Leaving past emissions in the supply would leave a permanent asterisk on the claim in A.4.1.2.2.2. Burning back to the counterfactual makes the rule true retroactively, which is what lets the Atlas state it without qualification.
description: When SKY Rewards emissions were replaced, an amount equal to all past emissions was burned so total supply matches a world where the emissions never happened — the same move for legacy conversions.
